title: Denoising score matching for the VP-SDE
goal:
Implement one evaluation of the continuous objective (Section 3.3, Equation 7) for the VP-SDE with the weighting $\lambda(t) = \sigma^2(t)$.

`dsm_loss(score_model, x0, t, eps)` takes a batch `x0` of shape `(batch, dim)`, times `t` of shape `(batch,)` in $(0, 1]$, and noise `eps` of shape `(batch, dim)`. Build $x(t) = m(t)\,x(0) + \sigma(t)\,\epsilon$ from the perturbation kernel (Appendix B, Equation 33), where $m(t) = e^{-\frac12\int_0^t\beta}$ and $\sigma^2(t) = 1 - e^{-\int_0^t\beta}$. The target is $\nabla_{x(t)} \log p_{0t}(x(t) \mid x(0)) = -(x(t) - m(t)\,x(0))/\sigma^2(t)$.

Return $\sigma^2(t)\,\|s_\theta(x(t), t) - \text{target}\|_2^2$, summed over the data dimensions and averaged over the batch. The model is called as `score_model(x_t, t)` and never sees `x0`.

The paper says to choose $\lambda \propto 1 / \mathbb{E}[\|\nabla \log p_{0t}\|_2^2]$ (Section 3.3). For this kernel that is $\lambda = \sigma^2(t)$.
hints: Compute the target from the noise: $-(x(t) - m\,x(0))/\sigma^2 = -\epsilon/\sigma$. Both forms give the same number.
`t` has one value per row. Reshape $m$ and $\sigma^2$ to `(batch, 1)` so they broadcast over the data dimensions.
Sum the squared error over the last axis, multiply by $\sigma^2(t)$ for each row, then average over the batch.
With $\lambda = \sigma^2$, predicting the score as $-\hat\epsilon/\sigma$ turns the loss into $\|\hat\epsilon - \epsilon\|^2$, the DDPM objective.
